# OPH reverse-engineering table: model and theorem premises

As of 2026-11-02. Generated from [the navigation map](../tracking/premise_register.json)
by `python tools/build_model_theorem_map.py`. Edit the input, then regenerate.

This map connects the canonical premise identifiers and active model obligations to their current construction evidence. It is navigation coverage, not an extraction of every paper or Lean antecedent and not a proof of discharge. Alternative branches retain their own hypotheses; cross-references do not change claim-registry dependency roles.

**Construct the simplest shared repair process satisfying the declared observational contract.** Architecture, observer services and the complete repair law can supply inputs. Their consequences need not be postulated again. A theorem attachment must identify the same states, instruments, retained records, access rules and scheduling domain; matching component formulas alone is insufficient. Unique selection of an implementation is separate from executing that implementation and testing its predictions.

The live construction is `model/`. Its native C/E instruments determine local exchange and coherence laws, finite stationary preparation, field and event-clock statistics, and complete quantum observation bounds. The finite transfer logarithm, local Liouville generator and modular action on a chosen algebra/reference are distinct constructions. An observer-relative clock is an accessible record process; no preferred universal physical clock is required. Supplied scalar, gauge and matter actions remain conditional benchmarks with their own occupation, temporal and spatial error contracts.

**Completion concerns observations.** The intended effective quantum-field, classical and gravitational descriptions must reproduce compatible joint statistics and intervention responses within controlled regimes. Fields, metrics and manifolds need not be fundamental objects. Native source execution does not by itself establish physical spacetime or identify a laboratory apparatus. Public oscillator comparisons retain their calibration, postselection, coordinate and sampling limitations; numerical agreement, mathematical consistency and code fidelity are separate from physical identification.

The entries distinguish finite executions, analytic bounds, imported theorem hypotheses and remaining physical attachments. Separate actions, preparations, detectors and approximation domains keep separate certificates. Reusing a theorem requires a valid map of its actual hypotheses, not a count of available results or the simultaneous imposition of incompatible branches.

The [current physical bridge](SOURCE_SELECTION.md#current-bridge-to-physical-observations) distinguishes finite observer field/clock results, the remaining effective QFT and spacetime identification, and actual public-data tests. No federation is required for the completed single-carrier calculations. Issue #1077 retains its original q=3 scalar-word deliverable; smaller executed histories do not replace it.

Many entries cite executable model packages that supply finite instances of a premise interface: overlapping-observer and incident-clock quantum correspondences, compiled apparatus words and a compiled clock history, the active event clock and the inverse clock, the native continuum operator and causal placement, record-law identification, finite equilibration and retrospective public-data attachment audits. Such a citation supplies a finite instance on a stated domain. It discharges no canonical premise, changes no disposition and promotes no retrospective comparison to a prospective test.

The exhaustive contract inventory below covers every registered claim and tracked Lean source module. Restricted same-model bindings retain all canonical inputs and require explicit domain maps before composition. Missing model realizations remain visible; coverage and typed compatibility do not certify scientific entailment or physical completion.

The finite interfaces in [SAME_PROCESS_INTERFACES.md](completion/SAME_PROCESS_INTERFACES.md) and model/completion/finite_attachment_map.json assign all 84 canonical rows to completion owners. They record 140 realized scoped attachments among 145 reviewed domains and zero canonical physical discharges. The source particle map records complete finite spectral certificates, exact radial eta currents, native stationary flavor coefficients and ordered-spin texture energy bounds. The retained P-dependent lepton coefficient is realized by a chosen current-gated memory and a localized native-current operator construction. Its design inputs, static/weak-pulse domain, prescribed texture and unresolved continuum/physical identification joins are explicit. No common interacting relativistic particle spectrum and Einstein model is proved. Source-selected nature couplings and physical defect assignments are not established. Retrospective comparisons add zero eligible prospective tests. Guarded compact texture transport, a common 180-mode interacting memory core and its hopping-work derivative are proved on declared finite source domains. A separate native 60-state link gives local non-Abelian Gauss constraints. No full physical particle spectrum, interacting chiral continuum or Einstein realization is established.

These groups are workgroup navigation crosswalks, not claim-consumer edges or changes
to proof status. A group links related construction, branch, downstream or metrology
work; that association does not make every listed premise an antecedent of every
listed theorem. Existing claim-registry edges and `explicit_non_consumer` declarations
remain authoritative. Physical attachments excluded by a theorem are not hidden premises
of that theorem. Group statuses describe the remaining connection, not whether a theorem
is proved; the constructed results are recorded separately below. This schema contains
no proof-discharge edges; the implementation status of each premise is the separate
[discharge table](#what-the-current-implementation-does-with-each-premise).

premise, and a theorem-library result holds on its premises whatever the status.

## Remaining-input and dependency rule

For a selected scope G, let I(g) denote each group's required inputs on its
declared family, state, observable algebra, clock, regime and quantitative error domain.
The remaining-input set is U(G) = union over g in G of I(g), with genuinely identical
inputs counted once. This is a bookkeeping rule, not a machine-computed logical set:
the prose, ordinary assumptions and imports require semantic review. Active
construction, optional branches, downstream physical attachments and metrology are
separate scopes; unioning them does not turn all of them into theorem antecedents.

A result H implies C discharges an input P only when C establishes P on that same
domain, with the required errors, and H has independent supplied or established
support. Substitution retains any outstanding inputs of H. Circular references,
a change of regulator/state/code, or an imported calibration relabeled as a derivation
do not close an obligation. Establishing a conditional theorem and realizing its
hypotheses in the candidate are distinct tasks. This tool checks neither entailment
nor acyclicity of scientific arguments and changes no existing dependency edges.

### RE-03: Scheduler, reference and resources

**Constructed:** Native counting and bounded scheduling results retain their declared reference and fairness/resource classes. The native observer declares its two-event tape and halting rule. The correctable-record evaluator gives 11 reachable terminal words and 16 prefixes under its binary preparation, with a lossless four-bit classical prefix encoding. On one carrier, complete even-load calibration laws reconstruct the unweighted structural response after dividing out each positive seam exposure. This removes uniform scheduling and fair-coin requirements for that structural readout; complete known preparations and full seam exposure remain. Deterministic even-load currents also permit exact reconstruction from 360 executed native shots, one per preparation/seam, without a probability-law oracle. This removes native sampling uncertainty for that protocol, not laboratory preparation or detector errors. A separate current-only binary calibration uses twelve spanning preparations and addressed seams. Its 110 stochastic settings have cap 24 and total timeout probability at most 55/4194304 under independent fair placement draws; 250 constant-current settings need one attempt each. The retained seeded execution uses 578 attempts. Both outcome values, rather than hidden coin records, support exact reconstruction under the declared fair law. Preparation/reset and record access remain inputs; the samples do not establish fairness. The exact marked incident/movement-clock law retains zero-current local hits, remote waits, field-conditioned continuations and feedback hits. For the uniform total-two single-port source, I/K tends to 33/5; an exact Poisson corrector supplies a finite conversion-error bound indexed by fixed global movement count, uniformly over initial states. The retained host record comparison preserves baseline acceptance and workload-control rejection under that conversion uncertainty without refitting. It does not transfer the ratio or calibration to the different root-clock product/canonical-sector field protocol, identify a physical clock, or authenticate the pseudorandom entropy. Ordered pair-clock means and terminal coincidences uniquely recover positive nonuniform IID seam weights on the native support. The normalization follows because each seam ticks exactly two ports. The inferred coverage alpha=30 min p_e supplies the finite warm-up bound; finite estimates require their own conservative exposure bounds. A cyclic control shares the means and coincidences but changes interval counts, exposing the independence premise.

Bounded native auxiliary selection and current-only full78 reset supply the elementary uniform binary sector jointly with its two initial public field bits. Exact positive success deficits give a complete reference-safe preparation error without successful-target normalization. The same carriers execute the incident-clock field/feedback protocol with all preparation, selection and waiting failures; the positive-transfer field dictionary is preserved within the combined bound. A common operational clock joins the retained native/field outputs. Two source-prepared faithful-reference hands retain their purifiers and all four final pointer outcomes. Their single calibration is Omega_ref=1/4 GeV; the entire field Hamiltonian and clock share lambda_j=1+j/4, so tau_eff=sum(lambda_j delta_tau). Clock and Ramsey ensemble probabilities give exact rational time and energy-gap intervals on explicit unaliased phase windows, without supplying the programmed duration or species energies to the inverse. Numerical source, conditioning, probability-grid and optional finite-shot errors are explicit. SI conversion uses hbar=h/(2 pi). Host runtime and native attempt counts are not physical time; a laboratory clock fit and absolute vacuum-energy zero are not inferred.

### RE-19: Matter, statistics and interactions

**Constructed:** This group remains open. Its source inventory supplies reusable finite and conditional field constructions, with explicit source/state/reference/clock domains. Detailed equations, exact constants and counterexamples live in those primary packages and the current field/mass research guides. The results below do not identify a common source merely because two constructions use the same particle vocabulary.

Internal currents and conditional particle dictionaries. Exact native port/current and exterior-algebra constructions provide twelve subgroup currents and the fifteen all-left-Weyl internal weights of one fermion family. Complete CAR embeddings, gauge Ward identities and invariant scalar/Yukawa tensors are implemented. A neutral scalar background gives seven Dirac colour/lepton components and one neutral left-Weyl field with conditional masses |v y| and left-only weak currents. Background values, generations and coefficients remain inputs. Centre classes alone lose full representations and fermion parity. Equal current representations, ordinary basis changes and repeated internal rows do not derive family multiplicity or measured mixing.

Declared finite controls and memory. Native pulse encodings implement current tomography, incidence-defined cooling, stationary references, complete C/E records, fixed-memory inversion and source energy/clock experiments. Their source-call, preparation, failure, buffer and controller domains are explicit. Preserving the classical repair law does not fix the coherent continuation or every detector. The native branch-algebra, rank/multiplicity and contracted-response tests delimit exact reducing codes on the specified carrier; they do not exclude enlarged, corrected or coherent architectures. Five-memory, cyclic-family and conditional P/MCPR coefficients have concrete declared implementations. Koide balance, phase selection, squared-effect dynamics and physical mass identification are separate statements. <a id="finite-contract-coverage"></a>

## Finite-contract coverage and compatible model connections

The complete machine inventory is the `model_supply.contract_coverage` section
of the [premise register](../tracking/premise_register.json). It retains every
canonical claim ID and tracked Lean module, all seven domain coordinates, every
binding's canonical assumptions/imports and every sourced connection map. The
[claim registry](../claims/claim_registry.yaml) owns statements, evidence and
premise roles; the [Lean sources](../Lean/) retain their quantified hypotheses.

Coverage includes non-theorem claims and is a superset of finite contracts.
Lexical declaration counts decide neither finiteness nor proof validity; Lean
builds remain responsible for kernel checks. Registry or source-module additions
require explicit inventory updates. All unbound claims have the same status:
**Open: no same-model instantiation recorded**. This does not invalidate a
theorem on its own fixture or add a physical premise to an explicit non-consumer.

Each binding is a restricted clause, not discharge of its whole registry row.
The JSON retains that row's complete assumption/import union, including inputs
outside the clause. The checker requires exact produced/consumed facts, acyclic
connections and a sourced map for every changed carrier, law, preparation,
record access, control, clock or regime coordinate. These are coverage and
contract checks: mathematical entailment requires review; strings and source
anchors are not proofs. No entry silently discharges a canonical premise.

| Coverage | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Canonical claims retained | 392 |
| Claims with restricted bindings | 67 |
| Claims with open common-model mapping | 325 |
| Tracked Lean source modules retained | 681 |
| Lean modules referenced by canonical evidence | 481 |
| Public theorem/lemma declarations | 12880 |
| Restricted bindings / sourced connections | 134 / 69 |
